answer: Because the food supply in the north is greater in summer
why: RSPB and Wikipedia say migrants come north for the summer food surge (insects, long days) and would not find enough food there in winter.
Nature (2001) measured heart rates in pelicans and found formation flight saves significant energy; Nature (2014) on ibis upwash agrees.

answer: Because no thermals form over the sea
why: Thermals form only over land, so soaring storks avoid sea crossings; both quotes come from Wikipedia (Bird migration, White stork), and no independent page that can be fetched was found.

answer: Because the migratory direction is innate
why: PLOS ONE (2016) tracked juvenile cuckoos and concluded that an innate migration programme guides them without adults; RSPB calls navigation 'hard-wired'.
Nat Geo and Wikipedia say the Arctic tern makes the longest migration of any bird or animal, Arctic to Antarctic and back each year.

Elephant calves weigh about 70–160 kg at birth (Wikipedia, Smithsonian, Nat Geo); no source found states the 'heaviest land-mammal newborn' superlative word for word, but no other land mammal comes close.
A newborn giraffe is 1.7–2 m tall (Wikipedia) and stands and walks within about an hour (San Diego Zoo).
Giant panda cubs weigh 90–130 g and are born pink, blind and hairless (Wikipedia, Smithsonian, Nat Geo); Smithsonian gives 1/900 of the mother's size where Wikipedia gives 1/800.
The 33-day gestation and jellybean size are the red kangaroo's figures (Australian Museum, Wikipedia).

Harvard Nutrition Source and the Whole Grains Council: the bran, germ and endosperm.
